item.title: Stable consumer prices in September: +1% year-on-year
item.description: On 1 October 2026, the FSO reported an unchanged CPI at 101.5 points in September: annual inflation of +1.0%, with fuel prices rising.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - CPI unchanged at 101.5 points in September 2026 - Annual inflation of 1% - Fuels and heating oil on the rise - Travel and hospitality down
## Key Facts - Published date → October 1, 2026 - Establishment → FSO - Index → 101.5 points - Base → December 2025 = 100 - Monthly comparison → unchanged - Annual inflation increase → +1.0%
## September data On 1 October 2026, the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) announced that the consumer price index (CPI) remained unchanged in September 2026 compared to the previous month. The index stood at 101.5 points, with December 2025 as a base of 100. For the monthly comparison, therefore, the overall level of the index did not change.
A comparison with the same month of the previous year offers a different result. The inflation increase was +1.0%, or 1%. The press release thus combines a stable monthly reading and a positive annual reading. The first measures the change compared to the previous month; the second compares September 2026 with the same month last year.
### A balance between different voices The monthly stability is a result of opposing trends that have offset each other. It does not mean that all the prices observed by the CPI have remained stationary. The overall movement has remained unchanged because some items have pushed up and others down.
Among the prices that have increased, the press release indicates heating oil, petrol and diesel. On the other hand, the prices of international flat-rate travel, car rental and car sharing, as well as those of the hotel and para-hotel sectors, have decreased. The source thus indicates both the rising and falling areas, without transforming the aggregate figure into an identical description for each expense.
For the reader, the practical point is to distinguish the CPI level from the individual components mentioned. An index that is stuck at 101.5 points in the month can coexist with different costs for heating, refuelling, travel or accommodation. The annual inflation of 1% adds a second perspective: the comparison with a year earlier. The press release and further information on the subject can be found on the FSO's website. The figure can be combined with costo della vita in Svizzera without confusing the monthly and annual comparisons. ## How to read the data in the balance sheet
### The average does not coincide with every expense For those who live or work in Switzerland, the unchanged CPI is a general reference, not a list that blocks all expenditure. The press release shows a compensation: the overall reading remains stationary, while the categories listed move in different directions. The practical consequence is simple: the same official figure can have a different weight depending on the expenses in the personal budget.
| Area indicated in the press release | Direction taken | |---|---| | Heating oil, petrol and diesel | On the rise | | International Flat-rate Travel | Decreasing | | Car rental and car sharing | Decreasing | | Hotel & Semi-Hotel Sectors | Decreasing |
The table separates two levels. Those who incur costs related to heating oil or fuel can look at the rising items; those who plan international flat-rate trips, use car rental or car sharing, or resort to hotels and para-hotel facilities, instead encounter categories indicated to be decreasing. The sign of the variation is therefore the figure to be read, not a figure to be automatically applied to one's spending.
The annual +1.0% should also be treated as a specific comparison. It tells how the CPI has moved compared to the same month of the previous year, while the monthly invariance describes the relationship with the previous month. Mixing the two horizons leads to a wrong reading: a balance sheet may not change in the last monthly comparison and, at the same time, be faced with a higher annual level.
To turn the data into an orderly check, it is advisable to compare your entries with the categories communicated by the FSO, without automatically extending the movement of one entry to all the others. The costo della vita in Svizzera offers a starting point for this practical reading.

### Three steps for a personal check 1. Record the time reference. Mark settembre 2026 as the period observed and 1 ottobre 2026 as the publication date. Beside it, note 101,5 points and the base dicembre 2025 = 100. The number thus remains linked to the period and base indicated by the source.
2. Separate the two comparisons. Create one row for the previous month, with an unchanged result, and one for the same month of the previous year, with an increase of +1,0%, equal to 1%. Do not use the annual figure as if it were the change over the last month.
3. Match expenses to the trends. Put the items related to heating oil, gasoline and diesel in one group. In another, put those related to international package tours, car rental, car sharing and hotel or para-hotel accommodation. The comparison serves to understand which items in your budget correspond to the movements described.
4. Check the original material. The press release and further information on the topic are available on the UST website. Use it as a reference to keep the monthly figure, the annual figure and the categories mentioned separate.
This procedure does not turn the CPI into a personal calculation: it organizes the comparison and prevents treating the index as if it described every single expense in the same way. For items not included in the list, it is advisable not to automatically assign a trend based solely on the press release. The interpretation thus remains faithful to the official data and its two time windows.

item.description: The cross-party committee calls for the tax disadvantage of married couples to be eliminated by maintaining the joint declaration. Vote on 29 November.

## In brief - The committee calls for the elimination of matrimonial tax disadvantage - The tax return would remain joint - The vote is set for November 29
## Key Facts - Proposal → eliminate disparity in direct federal tax - Joint → Declaration Template for Married Couples - Location → Bern - Implementation → three years for Parliament - Alternative → lower amount between joint and alternative calculation
## The committee presents the proposal
On Thursday, a cross-party committee in Bern presented the arguments in support of the initiative "Yes to fair federal taxes for married couples too - finally abolish marriage discrimination!" According to the initiators, the point to be corrected is the tax disadvantage that penalizes married couples.
The initiative, in the description provided by the committee, aims to eliminate the disparity in direct federal taxation. The proposed solution is defined as simple and fair and maintains a precise element: married couples would continue to file the joint tax return. For the reader who consults the dichiarazione delle imposte, the central reference is therefore the continuity of the joint return for spouses.
### The constitutional principle
The proposed constitutional article would set a criterion linked to the economic situation. When the situation is equal, a married couple should not pay a higher direct federal tax than an unmarried couple. The text also links this rule to the objective of preventing the tax system from favouring certain life patterns.
The committee compares its proposal with the individual taxation already decided. The difference indicated in the source concerns the way of submitting the return: in the model supported by the initiative, married couples would keep the joint tax return.
The committee summarises its approach in two related choices: eliminating the disparity in direct federal tax and retaining the joint return. The first concerns the tax result, the second the way in which income is presented.
The source then indicates the path for implementation. Parliament would have three years. If it does not intervene within that period, the Federal Council would have to introduce a transitional solution. For married couples, in that scenario, the lower tax amount between the joint calculation and the alternative calculation would be applied. The vote therefore concerns the principle indicated in the constitutional article, while the implementation modalities are placed in the next parliamentary passage.
The vote will take place on 29 November. This is the political step indicated by the committee after the presentation of the topics in Bern. ## The Comparison That Matters for Married Couples
The practical impact described by the initiative is that it keeps two elements together: the joint declaration remains, while the result of the direct federal tax should not be higher for a married couple than for an unmarried couple with the same economic situation. The committee therefore does not present the proposal as an abandonment of the joint declaration.
### Two scenarios in the proposal
To read the text without adding figures not contained in the source, the comparison can be ordered as follows:
| Scenario | Rule Described | |---|---| | Married couples | Joint tax return | | Economic equality | Direct federal tax not higher than for unmarried couples | | Failure to implement within three years | For married couples, lower amount between joint and alternative calculation |
The first element concerns the declaration form: the spouses would continue to file their tax returns together. The second concerns the criterion provided for in the constitutional article: with the same economic situation, marriage should not result in a higher direct federal tax.
The third element comes into play in the scenario indicated for parliamentary non-implementation. If parliament does not define the solution within three years, the Federal Council would have to introduce a transitional measure and apply the lower of the two calculations. The source therefore links the alternative calculation to that phase, not to the ordinary replacement of the joint declaration.
For households, the consequence to be followed is the distinction between principle and application. The principle is tax parity in the same economic situation; application would depend on the implementation path described. The source does not offer amounts or numerical examples: it therefore does not allow an individual saving to be estimated. A calcolatore delle imposte can help to organise a personal comparison, but it does not replace the criterion provided for in the proposal.
The timetable adds a concrete point. The vote is set for 29 November; after that, any implementation would have a parliamentary deadline of three years. If this deadline is not met, the Federal Council would have to introduce the transitional solution.

### Four concrete steps
1. Mark the date of the vote. The vote will be held on November 29th. It is the first operational reference for those who want to follow the initiative.
2. Check the subject of the proposal. The text concerns direct federal tax and aims to eliminate the disparity between married and unmarried couples with the same economic situation. The joint declaration, according to the proposal, would remain.
3. Separate the proposed model from individual taxation. The source presents the initiative as an alternative to the already decided individual taxation: for married couples, the model supported by the committee retains the joint tax return.
4. Follow the implementation deadline. If the text is implemented, Parliament would have three years to intervene. If it does not, the Federal Council would have to introduce a transitional solution based on the lowest tax amount between joint and alternative calculations.
These steps make it possible to read the news without confusing the vote with any subsequent application. The date of 29 November concerns the decision on the initiative; the three-year deadline concerns the implementation entrusted to Parliament. The Federal Council's solution is only suitable for the event that this deadline is not respected.
For a married couple, the verification to be kept in mind is therefore twofold. On the one hand, the proposal maintains the joint declaration. On the other hand, the constitutional article would set the limit that, in an equal economic situation, the direct federal tax should not be higher than that of an unmarried couple. The text links this approach to the objective of not favouring certain models of life.
The source does not provide individual amounts and does not describe numerical cases. ## In brief - As of 1 October 2026, five provisions will change in Switzerland - TJPG and TJPV aim to combat money laundering and terrorism - EES progressively digitises airport screening - EFTA-Kosovo and new rules for 30 km and 50 km
## Key Facts - TJPG and TJPV → October 1, 2026 - Foreign companies → branch, management or real estate in Switzerland - Titles → "Professional Bachelor" and "Master" - Borders → non-Schengen countries - EES → system - Agreement → FTA between EFTA States and Kosovo - Traffic-oriented roads → 50 km/h in principle - Urban areas → 30 km/h no longer on a large scale
As of 1 October 2026, five amendments on money laundering, tertiary level professional education and training, airport controls, trade with Kosovo and speed limits in localities will come into force in Switzerland. The overview includes the provisions and laws that have been applicable since the beginning of the month.
### Transparency and training
The first change concerns the Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Economically Beneficiary Persons, TJPG, and the related TJPV regulation. The two provisions are intended to improve the fight against money laundering and terrorism. Their scope also includes foreign companies when they have a branch in Switzerland, are managed here or own real estate in Switzerland. At the same time, new due diligence obligations apply to certain advisory activities, which involve, among others, lawyers and notaries, and in particular public limited companies, GmbH, cooperatives, certain investment companies and limited partnerships.
The revised Vocational and Professional Education and Training Act introduces the titles "Professional Bachelor" and "Master's degree". It makes post-diploma courses at specialist schools more flexible, allows English as the language of the examination and protects the term "Höhere Fachschule" by law.
### Borders, exchanges and roads
For those arriving at the airport from non-Schengen countries, the adapted regulation on the Entry and Exit System, EES, initiates the progressive digitalisation of the Schengen external borders. In the future, biometric data will be collected for third-country nationals; the Swiss authorities will be able to use new search alerts and information in the Schengen Information System, SIS. The EES replaces the previous manual passport checks with entry stamps and will digitally record when and where a third-country national enters or leaves.
The FTA between the EFTA states and Kosovo will increase legal certainty and predictability of bilateral trade, while improving access to the Kosovar market will gain better access to the Kosovo market. All existing Swiss exports to Kosovo will be exempt from customs duties, some of which will be subject to transitional periods.
Finally, the new amendments to the 30 km/h limit, linked to the "Schilliger motion", tabled almost five years ago, provide in principle for a limit of 50 km/h on traffic-oriented roads in localities. It is no longer possible to introduce the 30 km/h limit on a large scale in urban areas. Cities and municipalities that want to do so will have to prove by means of an expert report that there will be no diverted traffic on the streets of the districts. The five changes have different recipients. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical step is to understand whether the novelty concerns a corporate activity, a training course, a non-Schengen trip, an export to Kosovo or a municipal decision on traffic.
### The before and after comparison
For foreign companies, the source identifies three specific links to Switzerland: branch, land management or real estate. New due diligence obligations are to be considered for certain consultations; lawyers and notaries are among the professionals mentioned. The scope also includes public limited companies, GmbH, cooperatives and some investment and limited partnerships.
In the tertiary level vocational education programme, qualifications and organisation are changing: "Professional Bachelor" and "Master's" are coming, post-diploma courses are becoming more flexible, English is admitted to examinations and "Höhere Fachschule" is protected by law. For those who study, these are different elements to be checked in the same path.
For travellers, the difference between before and after is the transition from a manual passport check with a stamp to an electronic entry and exit record. The transition is progressive: those coming from non-Schengen countries must consider the new system, while the collection of biometric data for third-country nationals is suitable for the future. The SIS can also be used by the Swiss authorities with new alerts and information.
For trade with Kosovo, the effect is commercial: the FTA between the EFTA states and Kosovo increases legal certainty and predictability and improves access to the Kosovar market. Existing Swiss exports to Kosovo will be duty-free, partly after transitional periods.
In traffic, the comparison is between 50 km/h in principle on traffic-oriented roads and the use of 30 km/h, which can no longer be extended on a large scale in urban areas. A city or municipality that intends to introduce it on those roads must back up the choice with an expert opinion on the absence of diverted traffic in the districts. The Touring Club Schweiz (TCS) and the Automobil Club Schweiz (ACS) endorse this approach for traffic flow and network hierarchy, also mentioning public transport, fast e-bikes and emergency response organizations. To learn more about the mobility associated with this transition, see the mezzi pubblici. However, the two associations criticize low-noise road surfaces, which they consider to be more effective against noise.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. From an operational point of view, it is advisable to separate the date, subject and procedure. The same date does not produce the same action: for TJPG, TJPV and the 30 km/h limit, the entry into force is indicated on 1 October 2026; for EES, digitization is progressive and biometric data are planned in the future.
### Five-step checklist
1. Date and scope. Use October 1, 2026 as a reference for TJPG, TJPV, and new 30 km/h rules. For the airport system, consider a progression instead: EES replaces manual checks with digital enrollment, and biometric collection is set for the future.
2. Company or consultancy. If the subject is a foreign company, compare the situation with the three elements indicated: branch, management or real estate in Switzerland. If the activity is consultancy, check the new duty of care for certain activities; the source mentions lawyers and notaries among others. For the financial side, you can also consult the conti bancari in Svizzera.
3. Education. Tertiary level vocational education and training students can check which qualification they apply, the flexibility of post-diploma courses and the possibility of taking the exam in English. The term "Höhere Fachschule" is now protected by law.
4. Travel. If you are coming from a non-Schengen country, consider the gradual transition to the EES. The system will record when and where third-country nationals enter or leave; the Swiss authorities will be able to use new alerts and information in the SIS.
5. Export or viability. For exports to Kosovo, check the application of duty exemption and any transitional periods. If a city or municipality wants to introduce 30 km/h on a traffic-oriented road, the expert report must show that there will be no diverted traffic on the streets of the districts. To follow the effect on the personal budget, consult the costo della vita in Svizzera.
This distinction avoids confusing an educational qualification, a border procedure, a business rule, and a local decision. Once you've identified the change that affects you, use the calcolatore stipendio for a personal estimate.
